gloss: to stand in a row; to line a street (buildings)

definitions.gloss: to stand in a row; to be lined up (of buildings, structures)
definitions.explanation: Used to describe buildings, houses, or structures standing side by side along a street or in an area. Evokes a visual image of a row of structures.

examples.japanese: ビルが{建|た}ち{並|なら}ぶ。
{通|とお}りに{沿|そ}ってお{店|みせ}が{建|た}ち{並|なら}んでいる。
{駅前|えきまえ}には{高層|こうそう}マンションが{建|た}ち{並|なら}び、{昔|むかし}の{面影|おもかげ}はない。
examples.english: High-rise apartments line the area in front of the station, and there's no trace of what it used to look like.

notes:
A compound verb of {建|た}つ (to be built, to stand) and {並|なら}ぶ (to line up). Specifically used for buildings and structures, not for people standing in a line. Common in descriptions of cityscapes, neighborhoods, and street scenes.

TRANSITIVITY:
Intransitive — the buildings are the subject.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ビルが{建|た}ち{並|なら}ぶ — buildings line up
- {家|いえ}が{建|た}ち{並|なら}ぶ — houses stand in a row
- {建|た}ち{並|なら}ぶ{商店街|しょうてんがい} — a shopping street lined with stores

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {並|なら}ぶ — to line up (general, not specific to buildings)
- {立|た}ち{並|なら}ぶ — to stand in a row (for people or trees; uses {立|た}つ not {建|た}つ)
- {軒|のき}を{連|つら}ねる — to stand side by side (literary, for buildings)
